'''Giorgi Japaridze''' (also spelled Giorgie Dzhaparidze) is a [[Georgian-American]] researcher in [[logic]] and [[theoretical computer science]]. He currently holds the title of [[Full Professor]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://csc.villanova.edu/faculty/fullTime |title=Faculty : Villanova Dept of Computing Sciences |access-date=2015-06-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051030023049/http://csc.villanova.edu/faculty/fullTime |archive-date=2005-10-30 |url-status=dead }}</ref> at the Computing Sciences Department of [[Villanova University]]. Japaridze is best known for his invention of [[computability logic]], [[cirquent calculus]], and [[Japaridze's polymodal logic]].

== Research ==
During 1985–1988<ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://www.csc.villanova.edu/~japaridz/1988PolymodalProvLog.pdf The polymodal logic of provability]". Intensional Logics and Logical Structure of Theories. Metsniereba, Tbilisi, 1988, pages 16-48 (Russian).</ref> Japaridze elaborated the system GLP, known as [[Japaridze's polymodal logic]].<ref>G. Boolos, "[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/016800729390200W The analytical completeness of Japaridze's polymodal logics]". Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 61 (1993), pages 95-111.</ref><ref>L.D. Beklemishev, J.J. Joosten and M. Vervoort, "[https://web.archive.org/web/20111021134723/http://logcom.oxfordjournals.org/content/15/4/447.abstract A finitary treatment of the closed fragment of Japaridze's provability logic]". Journal of Logic and Computation 15(4) (2005), pages 447-463.</ref><ref>I. Shapirovsky, "[http://www.aiml.net/volumes/volume7/Shapirovsky.pdf PSPACE-decidability of Japaridze's polymodal logic]". Advances in Modal Logic 7 (2008), pages 289-304.</ref><ref>F. Pakhomov, "[https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs00153-014-0397-4 On the complexity of the closed fragment of Japaridze's provability logic]". Archive for Mathematical Logic 53 (2014), pages 949-967.</ref> This is a system of [[modal logic]] with the "necessity" operators [0],[1],[2],…, understood as a natural series of incrementally weak provability predicates for [[Peano arithmetic]]. In "The polymodal logic of provability"<ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://www.csc.villanova.edu/~japaridz/1988PolymodalProvLog.pdf The polymodal logic of provability]". Intensional Logics and Logical Structure of Theories. Metsniereba, Tbilisi, 1988, pages 16-48 (Russian).</ref> Japaridze proved the arithmetical completeness of this system, as well as its inherent incompleteness with respect to [[Kripke frame]]s. GLP has been extensively studied by various authors during the subsequent three decades, especially after [[Lev Beklemishev]], in 2004,<ref>L. Beklemishev, "[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0168007203001325 Provability algebras and proof-theoretic ordinals, I]". Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 128 (2004), pages 103-123.</ref> pointed out its usefulness in understanding the proof theory of arithmetic (provability algebras and [[proof-theoretic ordinal]]s).

Japaridze has also studied the [[first-order logic|first-order]] (predicate) versions of provability logic. He came up with an axiomatization of the single-variable fragment of that logic, and proved its arithmetical completeness and [[decidable problem|decidability]].<ref>G. Japaridze, "[https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF00401550 Decidable and enumerable predicate logics of provability]". Studia Logica 49 (1990), pages 7-21.</ref> In the same paper he showed that, on the condition of the 1-completeness of the underlying arithmetical theory, predicate provability logic with non-iterated modalities is [[recursively enumerable]]. In ''Studia Logica 50'' <ref>G. Japaridze, "[https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF00370393 Predicate provability logic with non-modalized quantifiers]". Studia Logica 50 (1991), pages 149-160.</ref> he did the same for the predicate provability logic with non-modalized quantifiers.

In 1992–1993, Japaridze came up with the concepts of [[cointerpretability]], [[tolerant sequence|tolerance]] and [[cotolerance]], naturally arising in [[interpretability logic]].<ref>G. Japaridze, "[https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF00370116 The logic of linear tolerance]". Studia Logica 51 (1992), pages 249-277.</ref><ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/016800729390201N A generalized notion of weak interpretability and the corresponding modal logic]". Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 61 (1993), pages 113-160.</ref> He proved that cointerpretability is equivalent to 1-conservativity and tolerance is equivalent to 1-consistency. The former was an answer to the long-standing [[open problem]] regarding the metamathematical meaning of 1-conservativity. Within the same line of research, Japaridze constructed the modal logics of tolerance<ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/016800729390201N A generalized notion of weak interpretability and the corresponding modal logic]". Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 61 (1993), pages 113-160.</ref> (1993) and of the [[arithmetical hierarchy]]<ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0168007294900639 The logic of arithmetical hierarchy]". Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 66 (1994), pages 89-112.</ref> (1994), and proved their arithmetical completeness.
In 2002 Japaridze introduced "the Logic of Tasks",<ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0168007201001233 The logic of tasks]". Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 117 (2002), pages 261-293.</ref> which later became a part of his Abstract Resource Semantics<ref>G. Japaridze, "[https://web.archive.org/web/20130429235343/http://logcom.oxfordjournals.org/content/16/4/489.abstract Introduction to cirquent calculus and abstract resource semantics]". Journal of Logic and Computation 16 (2006), pages 489-532.</ref><ref>I. Mezhirov and N. Vereshchagin, "[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002200000900097X On abstract resource semantics and computability logic]". Journal of Computer and Systems Sciences 76 (2010), pages 356-372.</ref> on one hand, and a fragment of Computability Logic (see below) on the other hand.

Japaridze is best known{{Citation needed|date=September 2015}} for founding [[Computability logic|Computability Logic]] in 2003 and making subsequent contributions to its evolution. This is a long-term research program and a semantical platform for "redeveloping logic as a formal theory of (interactive) computability, as opposed to the formal theory of truth that it has more traditionally been".<ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0890540111001076 Introduction to clarithmetic I]". Information and Computation 209 (2011), pages 1312-1354.</ref>
In 2006<ref>G. Japaridze, "[https://web.archive.org/web/20130429235343/http://logcom.oxfordjournals.org/content/16/4/489.abstract Introduction to cirquent calculus and abstract resource semantics]". Journal of Logic and Computation 16 (2006), pages 489-532.</ref> Japaridze conceived [[cirquent calculus]] as a proof-theoretic approach that manipulates graph-style constructs, termed cirquents, instead of the more traditional and less general tree-like constructs such as formulas or sequents. This novel proof-theoretic approach was later successfully used to "tame" various fragments of computability logic,<ref>G. Japaridze, "[https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00153-012-0313-8 The taming of recurrences in computability logic through cirquent calculus, Part I]". Archive for Mathematical Logic 52 (2013), pages 173-212.</ref><ref>G. Japaridze, "[https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00153-012-0314-7 The taming of recurrences in computability logic through cirquent calculus, Part II]". Archive for Mathematical Logic 52 (2013), pages 213-259.</ref> which had otherwise stubbornly resisted all axiomatization attempts using the traditional proof systems such as [[sequent calculus]] or [[Hilbert system|Hilbert-style systems]]. It was also used to (define and) axiomatize the purely propositional fragment of [[independence-friendly logic]].<ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://www.lmcs-online.org/ojs/viewarticle.php?id=717&layout=abstract From formulas to cirquents in computability logic]". Logical Methods is Computer Science 7 (2011), Issue 2, Paper 1, pages 1-55.</ref><ref>G. Japaridze, "On the system CL12 of computability logic". Logical Methods in Computer Science (in press).</ref><ref>W. Xu, "[http://jigpal.oxfordjournals.org/content/22/6/982 A propositional system induced by Japaridze's approach to IF logic]{{dead link|date=May 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}". Logic Journal of the IGPL 22 (2014), pages 982-991.</ref>
The birth of cirquent calculus was accompanied with offering the associated "abstract resource semantics". Cirquent calculus with that semantics can be seen as a logic of resources that, unlike [[linear logic]], makes it possible to account for resource-sharing. As such, it has been presented as a viable alternative to linear logic by Japaridze, who repeatedly has criticized the latter for being neither sufficiently expressive nor complete as a resource logic. This challenge, however, has remained largely unnoticed by the linear logic community, which never responded to it.{{Citation needed|date=September 2015}}

Japaridze has cast a similar (and also never answered) challenge to [[intuitionistic logic]],<ref>G. Japaridze, "[https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007%2F978-1-4020-9374-6_11 In the beginning was game semantics]". Games: Unifying Logic, Language and Philosophy. O. Majer, A.-V. Pietarinen and T. Tulenheimo, eds. Springer 2009, pages 249-350.</ref> criticizing it for lacking a convincing semantical justification the associated [[constructivism (philosophy of mathematics)|constructivistic]] claims, and for being incomplete as a result of "throwing out the baby with the bath water". [[Arend Heyting|Heyting]]'s intuitionistic logic, in its full generality, has been shown to be sound<ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://www.inf.u-szeged.hu/actacybernetica/edb/vol18n1/Japaridze_2007_ActaCybernetica.xml Intuitionistic computability logic] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017112707/http://www.inf.u-szeged.hu/actacybernetica/edb/vol18n1/Japaridze_2007_ActaCybernetica.xml |date=2017-10-17 }}". Acta Cybernetica 18 (2007), pages 77-113.</ref> but incomplete<ref>I. Mezhirov and N. Vereshchagin, "[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002200000900097X On abstract resource semantics and computability logic]". Journal of Computer and Systems Sciences 76 (2010), pages 356-372.</ref> with respect to the semantics of computability logic. The positive (negation-free) propositional fragment of intuitionistic logic, however, has been proven to be complete with respect to the computability-logic semantics.<ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0168007207000346 The intuitionistic fragment of computability logic at the propositional level]". Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 147 (2007), pages 187-227.</ref>
In "On the system CL12 of computability logic",<ref>G. Japaridze, "[https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0103 On the system CL12 of computability logic]". Logical Methods is Computer Science (in press).</ref> on the platform of computability logic, Japaridze generalized the traditional concepts of [[time complexity|time]] and [[space complexity|space]] complexities to interactive computations, and introduced a third sort of a complexity measure for such computations, termed "amplitude complexity".
Among Japaridze's contributions is the elaboration of a series of systems of (Peano) [[Peano arithmetic|arithmetic]] based on computability logic, named "[[clarithmetic]]s".<ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?verb=Display&version=1.0&service=UI&handle=euclid.jsl/1268917495&page=record Towards applied theories based on computability logic] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150629001449/http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?verb=Display&version=1.0&service=UI&handle=euclid.jsl%2F1268917495&page=record |date=2015-06-29 }}". Journal of Symbolic Logic 75 (2010), pages 565-601.</ref><ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0890540111001076 Introduction to clarithmetic I]". Information and Computation 209 (2011), pages 1312-1354.</ref><ref>G. Japaridze, "[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0168007213001115 Introduction to clarithmetic III]". Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 165 (2014), pages 241-252.</ref> These include complexity-oriented systems (in the style of [[bounded arithmetic]]) for various combinations of time, space and amplitude complexity classes.

==Biography and academic career==
Giorgi Japaridze was born in 1961 in [[Tbilisi]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] (then in the [[Soviet Union]]).
He graduated from [[Tbilisi State University]] in 1983, received a PhD degree (in philosophy) from [[Moscow State University]] in 1987, and then a second PhD degree (in computer science) from the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in 1998. During 1987–1992 Japaridze worked as a Senior Researcher at the Institute of Philosophy of the [[Georgian Academy of Sciences]]. During 1992–1993 he was a Postdoctoral Fellow at the [[University of Amsterdam]] (Mathematics and Computer Science department). During 1993–1994 he held the position of a visiting associate professor at the [[University of Notre Dame]] (Philosophy Department). He has joined the faculty of [[Villanova University]] (Computing Sciences Department). Japaridze has also worked as a visiting professor at [[Xiamen University]] (2007) and [[Shandong University]] (2010–2013) in [[China]].<ref>[http://www.csc.villanova.edu/~japaridz] Giorgi Japaridze's Homepage</ref>

==Awards==
In 1982, for his work "Determinism and Freedom of Will", Japaridze received a Medal from the Georgian Academy of Sciences for the best student research paper, granted to one student in the nation each year. In 2015, he received an Outstanding Faculty Research Award from Villanova University, granted to one faculty member each year.<ref>[http://www.philly.com/philly/news/298551161.html Villanova professor honored for research] (Philadelphia Inquirer article)</ref> Japaridze has been a recipient of various grants and scholarships, including research grants from the US [[National Science Foundation]], [[Villanova University]] and [[Shandong University]], Postdoctoral Fellowship from the Dutch government, [[Raymond Merrill Smullyan|Smullyan]] Fellowship from [[Indiana University]] (never utilized), and Dean's Fellowship from the [[University of Pennsylvania]].<ref>[http://www.csc.villanova.edu/~japaridz/study.html Giorgi Japaridze: Research and Publications]</ref>
